<?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8"?>
<!-- $Revision$ -->
<refentry xmlns="http://docbook.org/ns/docbook" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink" xml:id="function.sodium-crypto-box-seal-open">
 <refnamediv>
  <refname>sodium_crypto_box_seal_open</refname>
  <refpurpose>Anonymous public-key decryption</refpurpose>
 </refnamediv>

 <refsect1 role="description">
  &reftitle.description;
  <methodsynopsis>
   <type class="union"><type>string</type><type>false</type></type><methodname>sodium_crypto_box_seal_open</methodname>
   <methodparam><type>string</type><parameter>ciphertext</parameter></methodparam>
   <methodparam><modifier role="attribute">#[\SensitiveParameter]</modifier><type>string</type><parameter>key_pair</parameter></methodparam>
  </methodsynopsis>
  <simpara>
   Decrypt a message that was encrypted with <function>sodium_crypto_box_seal</function>
  </simpara>

 </refsect1>

 <refsect1 role="parameters">
  &reftitle.parameters;
  <variablelist>
   <varlistentry>
    <term><parameter>ciphertext</parameter></term>
    <listitem>
     <simpara>
      The encrypted message
     </simpara>
    </listitem>
   </varlistentry>
   <varlistentry>
    <term><parameter>key_pair</parameter></term>
    <listitem>
     <simpara>
      The keypair of the recipient. Must include the secret key.
     </simpara>
    </listitem>
   </varlistentry>
  </variablelist>
 </refsect1>

 <refsect1 role="returnvalues">
  &reftitle.returnvalues;
  <simpara>
   The plaintext on success, &return.falseforfailure;.
  </simpara>
 </refsect1>


 <refsect1 role="examples"><!-- {{{ -->
  &reftitle.examples;
  <example xml:id="sodium-crypto-box-seal-open.example.basic"><!-- {{{ -->
   <title><function>sodium_crypto_box_seal_open</function> example</title>
   <programlisting role="php">
<![CDATA[
<?php
// Ciphertext is not sensitive; base64_decode is fine
$sealed_b64 = "oRBXXAV4iQBrxlV4A21Bord8Yo/D8ZlrIIGNyaRCcGBfpz0map52I3xq6l+CST+1NSgQkbV+HiYyFjXWiWiaCGupGf+zl4bgWj/A9Adtem7Jt3h3emrMsLw=";
$sealed = base64_decode($sealed_b64);

// Keypair contains a cryptographic secret; use a timing-safe decoder
$keypair_b64 = "KZkF8wnB7bnC2aXB3lFOqCTc0Z6MllvaQb9ASVG8o2/MsewkuE4u1uaEgTzSakeiYyIW8DGj+02/L3cWIbs9bQ==";
$keypair = sodium_base642bin($keypair_b64, SODIUM_BASE64_VARIANT_ORIGINAL);

$opened = sodium_crypto_box_seal_open($sealed, $keypair);
var_dump($opened);
?>
]]>
   </programlisting>
   &example.outputs.similar;
   <screen>
<![CDATA[
string(41) "Writing software in PHP can be a delight!"
]]>
   </screen>
  </example><!-- }}} -->
 </refsect1><!-- }}} -->

</refentry>

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8"?>
<!-- $Revision$ -->
<refentry xmlns="http://docbook.org/ns/docbook" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink" xml:id="function.sodium-crypto-box-seal">
 <refnamediv>
  <refname>sodium_crypto_box_seal</refname>
  <refpurpose>Anonymous public-key encryption</refpurpose>
 </refnamediv>

 <refsect1 role="description">
  &reftitle.description;
  <methodsynopsis>
   <type>string</type><methodname>sodium_crypto_box_seal</methodname>
   <methodparam><modifier role="attribute">#[\SensitiveParameter]</modifier><type>string</type><parameter>message</parameter></methodparam>
   <methodparam><type>string</type><parameter>public_key</parameter></methodparam>
  </methodsynopsis>
  <simpara>
   Encrypt a message such that only the recipient can decrypt it.
  </simpara>
  <simpara>
   Unlike with <function>sodium_crypto_box</function>, you only need to know the recipient's
   public key to use <function>sodium_crypto_box_seal</function>. One consequence of this
   convenience, however, is that the ciphertext isn't bound to a static public key,
   and is therefore not authenticated. Hence, anonymous public-key encryption.
  </simpara>
  <simpara>
   <function>sodium_crypto_box_seal</function> still provides ciphertext integrity. Just not
   sender identity authentication.
  </simpara>
  <simpara>
   If you also need sender authentication, the <function>sodium_crypto_sign</function> functions
   are likely the best place to start.
  </simpara>

 </refsect1>

 <refsect1 role="parameters">
  &reftitle.parameters;
  <variablelist>
   <varlistentry>
    <term><parameter>message</parameter></term>
    <listitem>
     <simpara>
      The message to encrypt.
     </simpara>
    </listitem>
   </varlistentry>
   <varlistentry>
    <term><parameter>public_key</parameter></term>
    <listitem>
     <simpara>
      The public key that corresponds to the only key that can decrypt the message.
     </simpara>
    </listitem>
   </varlistentry>
  </variablelist>
 </refsect1>

 <refsect1 role="returnvalues">
  &reftitle.returnvalues;
  <simpara>
   A ciphertext string in the format of (one-time public key, encrypted message, authentication tag).
  </simpara>
 </refsect1>

 <refsect1 role="examples"><!-- {{{ -->
  &reftitle.examples;
  <example xml:id="sodium-crypto-box-seal.example.basic"><!-- {{{ -->
   <title><function>sodium_crypto_box_seal</function> example</title>
   <programlisting role="php">
<![CDATA[
<?php
$keypair = sodium_crypto_box_keypair();
$public_key = sodium_crypto_box_publickey($keypair);

// Obfuscated plaintext to make the example more fun
$plaintext_b64 = "V3JpdGluZyBzb2Z0d2FyZSBpbiBQSFAgY2FuIGJlIGEgZGVsaWdodCE=";
$decoded_plaintext = sodium_base642bin($plaintext_b64, SODIUM_BASE64_VARIANT_ORIGINAL);

$sealed = sodium_crypto_box_seal($decoded_plaintext, $public_key);
var_dump(base64_encode($sealed));

$opened = sodium_crypto_box_seal_open($sealed, $keypair);
var_dump($opened);
?>
]]>
   </programlisting>
   &example.outputs.similar;
   <screen>
<![CDATA[
string(120) "oRBXXAV4iQBrxlV4A21Bord8Yo/D8ZlrIIGNyaRCcGBfpz0map52I3xq6l+CST+1NSgQkbV+HiYyFjXWiWiaCGupGf+zl4bgWj/A9Adtem7Jt3h3emrMsLw="
string(41) "Writing software in PHP can be a delight!"
]]>
   </screen>
  </example><!-- }}} -->
 </refsect1><!-- }}} -->

</refentry>

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8"?>
<!-- $Revision$ -->
<refentry xmlns="http://docbook.org/ns/docbook" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink" xml:id="function.sodium-crypto-box-seed-keypair">
 <refnamediv>
  <refname>sodium_crypto_box_seed_keypair</refname>
  <refpurpose>Deterministically derive the key pair from a single key</refpurpose>
 </refnamediv>

 <refsect1 role="description">
  &reftitle.description;
  <methodsynopsis>
   <type>string</type><methodname>sodium_crypto_box_seed_keypair</methodname>
   <methodparam><modifier role="attribute">#[\SensitiveParameter]</modifier><type>string</type><parameter>seed</parameter></methodparam>
  </methodsynopsis>
  <simpara>
   Clamps the seed to form a secret key, derives the public key, and returns the two as a keypair.
  </simpara>
  <simpara>
   The <literal>*_seed_keypair</literal> functions are ideal for generating a keypair from a
   password and salt. Use the result as a <parameter>seed</parameter> to generate the desired keys.
  </simpara>

 </refsect1>

 <refsect1 role="parameters">
  &reftitle.parameters;
  <variablelist>
   <varlistentry>
    <term><parameter>seed</parameter></term>
    <listitem>
     <simpara>
      Some cryptographic input. Must be 32 bytes.
     </simpara>
    </listitem>
   </varlistentry>
  </variablelist>
 </refsect1>

 <refsect1 role="returnvalues">
  &reftitle.returnvalues;
  <simpara>
   X25519 Keypair (secret key and public key).
  </simpara>
 </refsect1>


</refentry>

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8"?>
<!-- $Revision$ -->
<refentry xmlns="http://docbook.org/ns/docbook" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink" xml:id="function.sodium-crypto-box">
 <refnamediv>
  <refname>sodium_crypto_box</refname>
  <refpurpose>Authenticated public-key encryption</refpurpose>
 </refnamediv>

 <refsect1 role="description">
  &reftitle.description;
  <methodsynopsis>
   <type>string</type><methodname>sodium_crypto_box</methodname>
   <methodparam><modifier role="attribute">#[\SensitiveParameter]</modifier><type>string</type><parameter>message</parameter></methodparam>
   <methodparam><type>string</type><parameter>nonce</parameter></methodparam>
   <methodparam><modifier role="attribute">#[\SensitiveParameter]</modifier><type>string</type><parameter>key_pair</parameter></methodparam>
  </methodsynopsis>
  <simpara>
   Encrypt a message using asymmetric (public key) cryptography.
  </simpara>
  <simpara>
   The algorithm used by functions prefixed with <function>sodium_crypto_box</function> are
   Elliptic Curve Diffie-Hellman over the Montgomery curve, Curve25519; usually abbreviated as
   X25519.
  </simpara>

 </refsect1>

 <refsect1 role="parameters">
  &reftitle.parameters;
  <variablelist>
   <varlistentry>
    <term><parameter>message</parameter></term>
    <listitem>
     <simpara>
      The message to be encrypted.
     </simpara>
    </listitem>
   </varlistentry>
   <varlistentry>
    <term><parameter>nonce</parameter></term>
    <listitem>
     <simpara>
      A number that must be only used once, per message. 24 bytes long.
      This is a large enough bound to generate randomly (i.e. <function>random_bytes</function>).
     </simpara>
    </listitem>
   </varlistentry>
   <varlistentry>
    <term><parameter>key_pair</parameter></term>
    <listitem>
     <simpara>
      See <function>sodium_crypto_box_keypair_from_secretkey_and_publickey</function>.
      This should include the sender's X25519 secret key and the recipient's X25519 public key.
     </simpara>
    </listitem>
   </varlistentry>
  </variablelist>
 </refsect1>

 <refsect1 role="returnvalues">
  &reftitle.returnvalues;
  <simpara>
   Returns the encrypted message (ciphertext plus authentication tag). The ciphertext will be
   16 bytes longer than the plaintext, and a raw binary string. See <function>sodium_bin2base64</function>
   for safe encoding for storage.
  </simpara>
 </refsect1>


</refentry>

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8"?>
<refentry xmlns="http://docbook.org/ns/docbook" xml:id="function.sodium-crypto-core-ristretto255-add">
 <refnamediv>

 <refsect1 role="description">

  <methodsynopsis>
   <type>string</type><methodname>sodium_crypto_core_ristretto255_add</methodname>
   <methodparam><type>string</type><parameter>p</parameter></methodparam>
   <methodparam><type>string</type><parameter>q</parameter></methodparam>

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8"?>
<refentry xmlns="http://docbook.org/ns/docbook" xml:id="function.sodium-crypto-core-ristretto255-from-hash">
 <refnamediv>
  <refname>sodium_crypto_core_ristretto255_from_hash</refname>
  <refpurpose>Maps a vector</refpurpose>
 </refnamediv>

 <refsect1 role="description">
  &reftitle.description;
  <methodsynopsis>
   <type>string</type><methodname>sodium_crypto_core_ristretto255_from_hash</methodname>
   <methodparam><type>string</type><parameter>s</parameter></methodparam>
  </methodsynopsis>
  <simpara>
   Maps a 64-bytes vector <parameter>s</parameter> to a group element.
   Available as of libsodium 1.0.18.
  </simpara>

  &warn.undocumented.func;
 </refsect1>

 <refsect1 role="parameters">
  &reftitle.parameters;
  <variablelist>
   <varlistentry>
    <term><parameter>s</parameter></term>
    <listitem>
     <simpara>
      A 64-bytes vector.
     </simpara>
    </listitem>
   </varlistentry>
  </variablelist>
 </refsect1>

 <refsect1 role="returnvalues">
  &reftitle.returnvalues;
  <simpara>
   Returns a 32-byte random &string;.
  </simpara>
 </refsect1>

 <refsect1 role="examples">
  &reftitle.examples;
  <example>
   <title><function>sodium_crypto_core_ristretto255_from_hash</function> example</title>
   <programlisting role="php">
<![CDATA[
<?php

$hashes = sodium_hex2bin(
    '5d1be09e3d0c82fc538112490e35701979d99e06ca3e2b5b54bffe8b4dc772c1' .
    '4d98b696a1bbfb5ca32c436cc61c16563790306c79eaca7705668b47dffe5bb6'
);
var_dump(sodium_bin2hex(sodium_crypto_core_ristretto255_from_hash($hashes)));
?>
]]>
   </programlisting>
   &example.outputs;
   <screen>
<![CDATA[
string(64) "3066f82a1a747d45120d1740f14358531a8f04bbffe6a819f86dfe50f44a0a46"
]]>
   </screen>
  </example>
 </refsect1>

 <refsect1 role="seealso">
  &reftitle.seealso;
  <simplelist>
   <member><function>sodium_hex2bin</function></member>
   <member><function>sodium_bin2hex</function></member>
   <member><function>sodium_crypto_core_ristretto255_from_hash</function></member>
  </simplelist>
 </refsect1>

</refentry>

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8"?>
<refentry xmlns="http://docbook.org/ns/docbook" xml:id="function.sodium-crypto-core-ristretto255-is-valid-point">
 <refnamediv>
  <refname>sodium_crypto_core_ristretto255_is_valid_point</refname>
  <refpurpose>Determines if a point on the ristretto255 curve</refpurpose>
 </refnamediv>

 <refsect1 role="description">
  &reftitle.description;
  <methodsynopsis>
   <type>bool</type><methodname>sodium_crypto_core_ristretto255_is_valid_point</methodname>
   <methodparam><type>string</type><parameter>s</parameter></methodparam>
  </methodsynopsis>
  <simpara>
   Determines if a point on the ristretto255 curve,
   in canonical form, on the main subgroup, and that the point doesn't have a small order.
   Available as of libsodium 1.0.18.
  </simpara>

  &warn.undocumented.func;
 </refsect1>

 <refsect1 role="parameters">
  &reftitle.parameters;
  <variablelist>
   <varlistentry>
    <term><parameter>s</parameter></term>
    <listitem>
     <simpara>
      An Elliptic-curve point.
     </simpara>
    </listitem>
   </varlistentry>
  </variablelist>
 </refsect1>

 <refsect1 role="returnvalues">
  &reftitle.returnvalues;
  <simpara>
   Returns &true; if <parameter>s</parameter> is on the ristretto255 curve, &false; otherwise.
  </simpara>
 </refsect1>

 <refsect1 role="examples">
  &reftitle.examples;
  <example>
   <title><function>sodium_crypto_core_ristretto255_is_valid_point</function> example</title>
   <programlisting role="php">
<![CDATA[
<?php

$foo = sodium_crypto_core_ristretto255_scalar_random();
$bar = sodium_crypto_scalarmult_ristretto255_base($foo);

var_dump(sodium_crypto_core_ristretto255_is_valid_point($bar));
?>
]]>
   </programlisting>
   &example.outputs;
   <screen>
<![CDATA[
bool(true)
]]>
   </screen>
  </example>
 </refsect1>

 <refsect1 role="seealso">
  &reftitle.seealso;
  <simplelist>
   <member><function>sodium_crypto_core_ristretto255_scalar_random</function></member>
   <member><function>sodium_crypto_scalarmult_ristretto255_base</function></member>
  </simplelist>
 </refsect1>

</refentry>

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8"?>
<refentry xmlns="http://docbook.org/ns/docbook" xml:id="function.sodium-crypto-core-ristretto255-scalar-invert">
 <refnamediv>
  <refname>sodium_crypto_core_ristretto255_scalar_invert</refname>
  <refpurpose>Inverts a scalar value</refpurpose>
 </refnamediv>

 <refsect1 role="description">
  &reftitle.description;
  <methodsynopsis>
   <type>string</type><methodname>sodium_crypto_core_ristretto255_scalar_invert</methodname>
   <methodparam><type>string</type><parameter>s</parameter></methodparam>
  </methodsynopsis>
  <simpara>
   Inverts a scalar value.
   Available as of libsodium 1.0.18.
  </simpara>

  &warn.undocumented.func;
 </refsect1>

 <refsect1 role="parameters">
  &reftitle.parameters;
  <variablelist>
   <varlistentry>
    <term><parameter>s</parameter></term>
    <listitem>
     <simpara>
      Scalar value.
     </simpara>
    </listitem>
   </varlistentry>
  </variablelist>
 </refsect1>

 <refsect1 role="returnvalues">
  &reftitle.returnvalues;
  <simpara>
   Returns a 32-byte random &string;.
  </simpara>
 </refsect1>

 <refsect1 role="examples">
  &reftitle.examples;
  <example>
   <title><function>sodium_crypto_core_ristretto255_scalar_invert</function> example</title>
   <programlisting role="php">
<![CDATA[
<?php

$foo = sodium_crypto_core_ristretto255_scalar_random();

$inverted = sodium_crypto_core_ristretto255_scalar_invert($foo);
$reInverted = sodium_crypto_core_ristretto255_scalar_invert($inverted);

var_dump(hash_equals($foo, $reInverted));
?>
]]>
   </programlisting>
   &example.outputs;
   <screen>
<![CDATA[
bool(true)
]]>
   </screen>
  </example>
 </refsect1>

 <refsect1 role="seealso">
  &reftitle.seealso;
  <simplelist>
   <member><function>sodium_crypto_core_ristretto255_scalar_random</function></member>
  </simplelist>
 </refsect1>

</refentry>

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8"?>
<refentry xmlns="http://docbook.org/ns/docbook" xml:id="function.sodium-crypto-core-ristretto255-scalar-random">
 <refnamediv>

   <void/>

 <refsect1 role="parameters">

  </simpara>

 <refsect1 role="examples">
  &reftitle.examples;
  <example>
   <title><function>sodium_crypto_core_ristretto255_scalar_random</function> example</title>
   <programlisting role="php">
<![CDATA[
<?php

$foo = sodium_crypto_core_ristretto255_scalar_random();
$bar = sodium_crypto_core_ristretto255_scalar_random();

var_dump(hash_equals($foo, $value));
?>

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8"?>
<!-- $Revision$ -->
<refentry xmlns="http://docbook.org/ns/docbook" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink" xml:id="function.sodium-crypto-generichash-final">
 <refnamediv>
  <refname>sodium_crypto_generichash_final</refname>
  <refpurpose>Complete the hash</refpurpose>
 </refnamediv>

 <refsect1 role="description">
  &reftitle.description;
  <methodsynopsis>
   <type>string</type><methodname>sodium_crypto_generichash_final</methodname>
   <methodparam><type>string</type><parameter role="reference">state</parameter></methodparam>
   <methodparam choice="opt"><type>int</type><parameter>length</parameter><initializer><constant>SODIUM_CRYPTO_GENERICHASH_BYTES</constant></initializer></methodparam>
  </methodsynopsis>
  <simpara>
   The finalization method for the streaming generichash API.
  </simpara>

 </refsect1>

 <refsect1 role="parameters">
  &reftitle.parameters;
  <variablelist>
   <varlistentry>
    <term><parameter>state</parameter></term>
    <listitem>
     <simpara>
      Hash state returned from <function>sodium_crypto_generichash_init</function>
     </simpara>
    </listitem>
   </varlistentry>
   <varlistentry>
    <term><parameter>length</parameter></term>
    <listitem>
     <simpara>
      Output length.
     </simpara>
    </listitem>
   </varlistentry>
  </variablelist>
 </refsect1>

 <refsect1 role="returnvalues">
  &reftitle.returnvalues;
  <simpara>
   Cryptographic hash.
  </simpara>
 </refsect1>

 <refsect1 role="examples"><!-- {{{ -->
  &reftitle.examples;
  <example xml:id="sodium-crypto-generichash-final.example.basic"><!-- {{{ -->
   <title><function>sodium_crypto_generichash_final</function> example</title>
   <programlisting role="php">
<![CDATA[
<?php
$messages = [random_bytes(32), random_bytes(32), random_bytes(16)];
$state = sodium_crypto_generichash_init('', 32);
foreach ($messages as $message) {
    sodium_crypto_generichash_update($state, $message);
}

$final = sodium_crypto_generichash_final($state, 32);
var_dump(sodium_bin2hex($final));

$allAtOnce = sodium_crypto_generichash(implode('', $messages));
var_dump(sodium_bin2hex($allAtOnce));
?>
]]>
   </programlisting>
   &example.outputs.similar;

   <methodparam><type>string</type><parameter>message</parameter></methodparam>

  </simpara>

 </refsect1>

 <refsect1 role="parameters">

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8"?>
<!-- $Revision$ -->
<refentry xmlns="http://docbook.org/ns/docbook" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink" xml:id="function.sodium-crypto-generichash">
 <refnamediv>
  <refname>sodium_crypto_generichash</refname>
  <refpurpose>Get a hash of the message</refpurpose>
 </refnamediv>

 <refsect1 role="description">
  &reftitle.description;
  <methodsynopsis>
   <type>string</type><methodname>sodium_crypto_generichash</methodname>
   <methodparam><type>string</type><parameter>message</parameter></methodparam>
   <methodparam choice="opt"><modifier role="attribute">#[\SensitiveParameter]</modifier><type>string</type><parameter>key</parameter><initializer>""</initializer></methodparam>
   <methodparam choice="opt"><type>int</type><parameter>length</parameter><initializer><constant>SODIUM_CRYPTO_GENERICHASH_BYTES</constant></initializer></methodparam>
  </methodsynopsis>
  <simpara>
   Hash a message with BLAKE2b.
  </simpara>

 </refsect1>

 <refsect1 role="parameters">
  &reftitle.parameters;
  <variablelist>
   <varlistentry>
    <term><parameter>message</parameter></term>
    <listitem>
     <simpara>
      The message being hashed.
     </simpara>
    </listitem>
   </varlistentry>
   <varlistentry>
    <term><parameter>key</parameter></term>
    <listitem>
     <simpara>
      (Optional) cryptographic key. This serves the same function as a HMAC key, but it's
      utilized as a reserved section of the internal BLAKE2 state.
     </simpara>
    </listitem>
   </varlistentry>
   <varlistentry>
    <term><parameter>length</parameter></term>
    <listitem>
     <simpara>
      Output size.
     </simpara>
    </listitem>
   </varlistentry>
  </variablelist>
 </refsect1>

 <refsect1 role="returnvalues">
  &reftitle.returnvalues;
  <simpara>
   The cryptographic hash as raw bytes. If a hex-encoded output is desired,
   the result can be passed to <function>sodium_bin2hex</function>.
  </simpara>
 </refsect1>


</refentry>

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8"?>

<refentry xmlns="http://docbook.org/ns/docbook" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink" xml:id="function.sodium-crypto-kdf-derive-from-key">
 <refnamediv>

 </refnamediv>

 <refsect1 role="description">
  &reftitle.description;
  <methodsynopsis>
   <type>string</type><methodname>sodium_crypto_kdf_derive_from_key</methodname>

   <methodparam><type>int</type><parameter>subkey_id</parameter></methodparam>

   <methodparam><modifier role="attribute">#[\SensitiveParameter]</modifier><type>string</type><parameter>key</parameter></methodparam>
  </methodsynopsis>
  <simpara>
   Derive a subkey from a root key and additional context.
  </simpara>
  <simpara>

  </simpara>

 </refsect1>

 <refsect1 role="parameters">
  &reftitle.parameters;
  <variablelist>
   <varlistentry>
    <term><parameter>subkey_length</parameter></term>
    <listitem>

    </listitem>
   </varlistentry>
   <varlistentry>
    <term><parameter>subkey_id</parameter></term>
    <listitem>
     <simpara>

     </simpara>
    </listitem>
   </varlistentry>
   <varlistentry>
    <term><parameter>context</parameter></term>
    <listitem>

   </varlistentry>
  </variablelist>
 </refsect1>

 <refsect1 role="returnvalues">
  &reftitle.returnvalues;
  <simpara>
   A string of pseudorandom (raw binary) bytes.
  </simpara>
 </refsect1>

<refentry xmlns="http://docbook.org/ns/docbook" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink" xml:id="function.sodium-crypto-kx-client-session-keys">
 <refnamediv>
  <refname>sodium_crypto_kx_client_session_keys</refname>

 </refnamediv>

 <refsect1 role="description">
  &reftitle.description;
  <methodsynopsis>
   <type>array</type><methodname>sodium_crypto_kx_client_session_keys</methodname>

   <methodparam><type>string</type><parameter>server_key</parameter></methodparam>
  </methodsynopsis>
  <simpara>
   Calculate the client-side session keys, using the X25519 + BLAKE2b key-exchange method.
  </simpara>

 </refsect1>

  &reftitle.parameters;
  <variablelist>

     </simpara>
    </listitem>
   </varlistentry>

    <term><parameter>server_key</parameter></term>

  </simpara>

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8"?>
<!-- $Revision$ -->
<refentry xmlns="http://docbook.org/ns/docbook" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink" xml:id="function.sodium-crypto-kx-keypair">
 <refnamediv>
  <refname>sodium_crypto_kx_keypair</refname>
  <refpurpose>Creates a new sodium keypair</refpurpose>
 </refnamediv>

 <refsect1 role="description">
  &reftitle.description;
  <methodsynopsis>
   <type>string</type><methodname>sodium_crypto_kx_keypair</methodname>
   <void/>
  </methodsynopsis>
  <simpara>
   Create a new sodium keypair consisting of the secret key (32 bytes)
   followed by the public key (32 bytes). The keys can be retrieved by calling
   <function>sodium_crypto_kx_secretkey</function> and
   <function>sodium_crypto_kx_publickey</function>, respectively.
  </simpara>
 </refsect1>

 <refsect1 role="parameters">
  &reftitle.parameters;
  &no.function.parameters;
 </refsect1>

 <refsect1 role="returnvalues">
  &reftitle.returnvalues;
  <simpara>
   Returns the new keypair on success; throws an exception otherwise.
  </simpara>
 </refsect1>

 <refsect1 role="examples">
  &reftitle.examples;
  <example xml:id="sodium-crypto-kx-keypair.example.basic">
   <title><function>sodium_crypto_kx_keypair</function> usage</title>
   <simpara>
     Create a new keypair and retrieve the secret and the public key from it.
   </simpara>
   <programlisting role="php">
<![CDATA[
<?php
$keypair = sodium_crypto_kx_keypair();
$secret = sodium_crypto_kx_secretkey($keypair);
$public = sodium_crypto_kx_publickey($keypair);
printf("secret: %s\npublic: %s", sodium_bin2hex($secret), sodium_bin2hex($public));
?>
]]>
   </programlisting>
   &example.outputs.similar;
   <screen>
<![CDATA[
secret: e7c5c918fdc40762e6000542c0118f4368ce8fd242b0e48c1e17202797a25daf
public: d1f59fda8652caf40ed1a01d2b6f3802b60846986372cd8fa337b7c12c428b18
]]>
   </screen>
  </example>
 </refsect1>

</refentry>

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8"?>
<!-- $Revision$ -->
<refentry xmlns="http://docbook.org/ns/docbook" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink" xml:id="function.sodium-crypto-pwhash-scryptsalsa208sha256">
 <refnamediv>
  <refname>sodium_crypto_pwhash_scryptsalsa208sha256</refname>
  <refpurpose>Derives a key from a password, using scrypt</refpurpose>
 </refnamediv>

 <refsect1 role="description">
  &reftitle.description;
  <methodsynopsis>
   <type>string</type><methodname>sodium_crypto_pwhash_scryptsalsa208sha256</methodname>
   <methodparam><type>int</type><parameter>length</parameter></methodparam>
   <methodparam><modifier role="attribute">#[\SensitiveParameter]</modifier><type>string</type><parameter>password</parameter></methodparam>
   <methodparam><type>string</type><parameter>salt</parameter></methodparam>
   <methodparam><type>int</type><parameter>opslimit</parameter></methodparam>
   <methodparam><type>int</type><parameter>memlimit</parameter></methodparam>
  </methodsynopsis>
  <simpara>
   This is the scrypt counterpart to <function>sodium_crypto_pwhash</function>.
  </simpara>
  <simpara>
   A common reason to use this particular function is to derive the seeds for cryptographic keys from a password and salt,
   and then use these seeds to generate the actual keys needed for some purpose (e.g. <function>sodium_crypto_sign_detached</function>).
  </simpara>

 </refsect1>

 <refsect1 role="parameters">
  &reftitle.parameters;
  <variablelist>
   <varlistentry>
    <term><parameter>length</parameter></term>
    <listitem>
     <simpara>
      The length of the password hash to generate, in bytes.
     </simpara>
    </listitem>
   </varlistentry>
   <varlistentry>
    <term><parameter>password</parameter></term>
    <listitem>
     <simpara>
      The password to generate a hash for.
     </simpara>
    </listitem>
   </varlistentry>
   <varlistentry>
    <term><parameter>salt</parameter></term>
    <listitem>
     <simpara>
      A salt to add to the password before hashing. The salt should be unpredictable, ideally generated from a good random number source such as <function>random_bytes</function>, and have a length of at least <constant>SODIUM_CRYPTO_PWHASH_SCRYPTSALSA208SHA256_SALTBYTES</constant> bytes.
     </simpara>
    </listitem>
   </varlistentry>
   <varlistentry>
    <term><parameter>opslimit</parameter></term>
    <listitem>
     <simpara>
      Represents a maximum amount of computations to perform. Raising this number will make the function require more CPU cycles to compute a key. There are some constants available to set the operations limit to appropriate values depending on intended use, in order of strength: <constant>SODIUM_CRYPTO_PWHASH_SCRYPTSALSA208SHA256_OPSLIMIT_INTERACTIVE</constant> and <constant>SODIUM_CRYPTO_PWHASH_SCRYPTSALSA208SHA256_OPSLIMIT_SENSITIVE</constant>.
     </simpara>
    </listitem>
   </varlistentry>
   <varlistentry>
    <term><parameter>memlimit</parameter></term>
    <listitem>
     <simpara>
      The maximum amount of RAM that the function will use, in bytes. There are constants to help you choose an appropriate value, in order of size: <constant>SODIUM_CRYPTO_PWHASH_SCRYPTSALSA208SHA256_MEMLIMIT_INTERACTIVE</constant> and <constant>SODIUM_CRYPTO_PWHASH_SCRYPTSALSA208SHA256_MEMLIMIT_SENSITIVE</constant>. Typically these should be paired with the matching <parameter>opslimit</parameter> values.
     </simpara>
    </listitem>
   </varlistentry>
  </variablelist>
 </refsect1>

 <refsect1 role="returnvalues">
  &reftitle.returnvalues;
  <simpara>
   A string of bytes of the desired length.
  </simpara>
 </refsect1>


</refentry>

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8"?>
<!-- $Revision$ -->
<refentry xmlns="http://docbook.org/ns/docbook" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink" xml:id="function.sodium-crypto-pwhash-str-needs-rehash">
 <refnamediv>
  <refname>sodium_crypto_pwhash_str_needs_rehash</refname>
  <refpurpose>Determine whether or not to rehash a password</refpurpose>
 </refnamediv>

 <refsect1 role="description">
  &reftitle.description;
  <methodsynopsis>
   <type>bool</type><methodname>sodium_crypto_pwhash_str_needs_rehash</methodname>
   <methodparam><type>string</type><parameter>password</parameter></methodparam>
   <methodparam><type>int</type><parameter>opslimit</parameter></methodparam>
   <methodparam><type>int</type><parameter>memlimit</parameter></methodparam>
  </methodsynopsis>
  <simpara>
   Determine whether or not to rehash a password, based on the current hash <parameter>opslimit</parameter> and <parameter>memlimit</parameter>.
  </simpara>

 </refsect1>

 <refsect1 role="parameters">
  &reftitle.parameters;
  <variablelist>
   <varlistentry>
    <term><parameter>password</parameter></term>
    <listitem>
     <simpara>
      Password hash
     </simpara>
    </listitem>
   </varlistentry>
   <varlistentry>
    <term><parameter>opslimit</parameter></term>
    <listitem>
     <simpara>
      Configured opslimit; see <function>sodium_crypto_pwhash_str</function>
     </simpara>
    </listitem>
   </varlistentry>
   <varlistentry>
    <term><parameter>memlimit</parameter></term>
    <listitem>
     <simpara>
      Configured memlimit; see <function>sodium_crypto_pwhash_str</function>
     </simpara>
    </listitem>
   </varlistentry>
  </variablelist>
 </refsect1>

 <refsect1 role="returnvalues">
  &reftitle.returnvalues;
  <simpara>
   Returns &true; if the provided memlimit/opslimit do not match what's stored in the hash.
   Returns &false; if they match.
  </simpara>
 </refsect1>


</refentry>

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8"?>
<!-- $Revision$ -->
<refentry xmlns="http://docbook.org/ns/docbook" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink" xml:id="function.sodium-crypto-pwhash-str-verify">
 <refnamediv>
  <refname>sodium_crypto_pwhash_str_verify</refname>
  <refpurpose>Verifies that a password matches a hash</refpurpose>
 </refnamediv>

 <refsect1 role="description">
  &reftitle.description;
  <methodsynopsis>
   <type>bool</type><methodname>sodium_crypto_pwhash_str_verify</methodname>
   <methodparam><type>string</type><parameter>hash</parameter></methodparam>
   <methodparam><modifier role="attribute">#[\SensitiveParameter]</modifier><type>string</type><parameter>password</parameter></methodparam>
  </methodsynopsis>
  <simpara>
   Checks that a password hash created using <function>sodium_crypto_pwhash_str</function> matches a given plain-text password. Note that the parameters are in the opposite order to the same parameters in the similar <function>password_verify</function> function.
  </simpara>


 </refsect1>

 <refsect1 role="parameters">
  &reftitle.parameters;
  <variablelist>
   <varlistentry>
    <term><parameter>hash</parameter></term>
    <listitem>
     <simpara>
      &password.parameter.hash;
     </simpara>
    </listitem>
   </varlistentry>
   <varlistentry>
    <term><parameter>password</parameter></term>
    <listitem>
     <simpara>
      &password.parameter.password;
     </simpara>
    </listitem>
   </varlistentry>
  </variablelist>
 </refsect1>

 <refsect1 role="returnvalues">
  &reftitle.returnvalues;
  <simpara>
   Returns &true; if the password and hash match, or &false; otherwise.
  </simpara>
 </refsect1>

 <refsect1 role="notes">
  &reftitle.notes;
  <note>
   <simpara>
    Hashes are calculated using the Argon2ID algorithm, providing resistance to both GPU and side-channel attacks.
   </simpara>
  </note>
 </refsect1>

 <refsect1 role="seealso">
  &reftitle.seealso;
  <simplelist>
   <member><function>sodium_crypto_pwhash_str</function></member>
   <member><function>password_hash</function></member>
   <member><function>password_verify</function></member>
  </simplelist>
 </refsect1>

</refentry>

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8"?>
<!-- $Revision$ -->
<refentry xmlns="http://docbook.org/ns/docbook" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink" xml:id="function.sodium-crypto-pwhash-str">
 <refnamediv>
  <refname>sodium_crypto_pwhash_str</refname>
  <refpurpose>Get an ASCII-encoded hash</refpurpose>
 </refnamediv>

 <refsect1 role="description">
  &reftitle.description;
  <methodsynopsis>
   <type>string</type><methodname>sodium_crypto_pwhash_str</methodname>
   <methodparam><modifier role="attribute">#[\SensitiveParameter]</modifier><type>string</type><parameter>password</parameter></methodparam>
   <methodparam><type>int</type><parameter>opslimit</parameter></methodparam>
   <methodparam><type>int</type><parameter>memlimit</parameter></methodparam>
  </methodsynopsis>
  <simpara>
Uses a CPU- and memory-hard hash algorithm along with a randomly-generated salt, and memory and CPU limits to generate an ASCII-encoded hash suitable for password storage.
  </simpara>
 </refsect1>

 <refsect1 role="parameters">
  &reftitle.parameters;
  <variablelist>
   <varlistentry>
    <term><parameter>password</parameter></term>
    <listitem>
     <simpara>
      <type>string</type>; The password to generate a hash for.
     </simpara>
    </listitem>
   </varlistentry>
   <varlistentry>
    <term><parameter>opslimit</parameter></term>
    <listitem>
     <simpara>
      Represents a maximum amount of computations to perform. Raising this number will make the function require more CPU cycles to compute a key. There are constants available to set the operations limit to appropriate values depending on intended use, in order of strength: <constant>SODIUM_CRYPTO_PWHASH_OPSLIMIT_INTERACTIVE</constant>, <constant>SODIUM_CRYPTO_PWHASH_OPSLIMIT_MODERATE</constant> and <constant>SODIUM_CRYPTO_PWHASH_OPSLIMIT_SENSITIVE</constant>.
     </simpara>
    </listitem>
   </varlistentry>
   <varlistentry>
    <term><parameter>memlimit</parameter></term>
    <listitem>
     <simpara>
      The maximum amount of RAM that the function will use, in bytes. There are constants to help you choose an appropriate value, in order of size: <constant>SODIUM_CRYPTO_PWHASH_MEMLIMIT_INTERACTIVE</constant>, <constant>SODIUM_CRYPTO_PWHASH_MEMLIMIT_MODERATE</constant>, and <constant>SODIUM_CRYPTO_PWHASH_MEMLIMIT_SENSITIVE</constant>. Typically these should be paired with the matching opslimit values.
     </simpara>
    </listitem>
   </varlistentry>
  </variablelist>
 </refsect1>

 <refsect1 role="returnvalues">
  &reftitle.returnvalues;
  <simpara>
   Returns the hashed password.
  </simpara>
  <simpara>
   In order to produce the same password hash from the same password, the same values for <parameter>opslimit</parameter> and <parameter>memlimit</parameter> must be used. These are embedded within the generated hash, so
   everything that's needed to verify the hash is included. This allows
   the <function>sodium_crypto_pwhash_str_verify</function> function to verify the hash without
   needing separate storage for the other parameters.
  </simpara>
 </refsect1>

  <refsect1 role="examples">
  &reftitle.examples;
  <example>
   <title><function>sodium_crypto_pwhash_str</function> example</title>
   <programlisting role="php">
<![CDATA[
<?php
$password = 'password';
echo sodium_crypto_pwhash_str(
    $password,
    SODIUM_CRYPTO_PWHASH_OPSLIMIT_INTERACTIVE,
    SODIUM_CRYPTO_PWHASH_MEMLIMIT_INTERACTIVE
);
]]>
   </programlisting>
   &example.outputs.similar;
   <screen>
<![CDATA[
$argon2id$v=19$m=65536,t=2,p=1$oWIfdaXwWwhVmovOBc2NAQ$EbsZ+JnZyyavkafS0hoc4HdaOB0ILWZESAZ7kVGa+Iw
]]>
   </screen>
  </example>
 </refsect1>

 <refsect1 role="notes">
  &reftitle.notes;
  <note>
   <simpara>
    Hashes are calculated using the Argon2ID algorithm,
    providing resistance to both GPU and side-channel attacks.
    In contrast to the <function>password_hash</function> function,
    there is no salt parameter (a salt is generated automatically),
    and the <parameter>opslimit</parameter> and
    <parameter>memlimit</parameter> parameters are not optional.
   </simpara>
  </note>
 </refsect1>

 <refsect1 role="seealso">
  &reftitle.seealso;
  <simplelist>
   <member><function>sodium_crypto_pwhash_str_verify</function></member>
   <member><function>sodium_crypto_pwhash</function></member>
   <member><function>password_hash</function></member>
   <member><function>password_verify</function></member>
   <member><link xlink:href="&url.libsodium.argon2;">Libsodium Argon2 docs</link></member>
  </simplelist>
 </refsect1>


</refentry>

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8"?>
<!-- $Revision$ -->
<refentry xmlns="http://docbook.org/ns/docbook" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink" xml:id="function.sodium-crypto-pwhash">
 <refnamediv>
  <refname>sodium_crypto_pwhash</refname>
  <refpurpose>Derive a key from a password, using Argon2</refpurpose>
 </refnamediv>

 <refsect1 role="description">
  &reftitle.description;
  <methodsynopsis>
   <type>string</type><methodname>sodium_crypto_pwhash</methodname>
   <methodparam><type>int</type><parameter>length</parameter></methodparam>
   <methodparam><modifier role="attribute">#[\SensitiveParameter]</modifier><type>string</type><parameter>password</parameter></methodparam>
   <methodparam><type>string</type><parameter>salt</parameter></methodparam>
   <methodparam><type>int</type><parameter>opslimit</parameter></methodparam>
   <methodparam><type>int</type><parameter>memlimit</parameter></methodparam>
   <methodparam choice="opt"><type>int</type><parameter>algo</parameter><initializer><constant>SODIUM_CRYPTO_PWHASH_ALG_DEFAULT</constant></initializer></methodparam>
  </methodsynopsis>
  <simpara>
   This function provides low-level access to libsodium's crypto_pwhash key derivation function. Unless you have specific reason to use this function, you should use <function>sodium_crypto_pwhash_str</function> or <function>password_hash</function> functions instead.
  </simpara>
  <simpara>
   A common reason to use this particular function is to derive the seeds for cryptographic keys from a password and salt,
   and then use these seeds to generate the actual keys needed for some purpose (e.g. <function>sodium_crypto_sign_detached</function>).
  </simpara>
 </refsect1>

 <refsect1 role="parameters">
  &reftitle.parameters;
  <variablelist>
   <varlistentry>
    <term><parameter>length</parameter></term>
    <listitem>
     <simpara>
      <type>int</type>; The length of the password hash to generate, in bytes.
     </simpara>
    </listitem>
   </varlistentry>
   <varlistentry>
    <term><parameter>password</parameter></term>
    <listitem>
     <simpara>
      <type>string</type>; The password to generate a hash for.
     </simpara>
    </listitem>
   </varlistentry>
   <varlistentry>
    <term><parameter>salt</parameter></term>
    <listitem>
     <simpara>
      A salt to add to the password before hashing. The salt should be unpredictable, ideally generated from a good random number source such as <function>random_bytes</function>, and have a length of exactly <constant>SODIUM_CRYPTO_PWHASH_SALTBYTES</constant> bytes.
     </simpara>
    </listitem>
   </varlistentry>
   <varlistentry>
    <term><parameter>opslimit</parameter></term>
    <listitem>
     <simpara>
      Represents a maximum amount of computations to perform. Raising this number will make the function require more CPU cycles to compute a key. There are some constants available to set the operations limit to appropriate values depending on intended use, in order of strength: <constant>SODIUM_CRYPTO_PWHASH_OPSLIMIT_INTERACTIVE</constant>, <constant>SODIUM_CRYPTO_PWHASH_OPSLIMIT_MODERATE</constant> and <constant>SODIUM_CRYPTO_PWHASH_OPSLIMIT_SENSITIVE</constant>.
     </simpara>
    </listitem>
   </varlistentry>
   <varlistentry>
    <term><parameter>memlimit</parameter></term>
    <listitem>
     <simpara>
      The maximum amount of RAM that the function will use, in bytes. There are constants to help you choose an appropriate value, in order of size: <constant>SODIUM_CRYPTO_PWHASH_MEMLIMIT_INTERACTIVE</constant>, <constant>SODIUM_CRYPTO_PWHASH_MEMLIMIT_MODERATE</constant>, and <constant>SODIUM_CRYPTO_PWHASH_MEMLIMIT_SENSITIVE</constant>. Typically these should be paired with the matching <parameter>opslimit</parameter> values.
     </simpara>
    </listitem>
   </varlistentry>
   <varlistentry>
    <term><parameter>algo</parameter></term>
    <listitem>
     <simpara>
      <type>int</type> A number indicating the hash algorithm to use. By default <constant>SODIUM_CRYPTO_PWHASH_ALG_DEFAULT</constant> (the currently recommended algorithm, which can change from one version of libsodium to another), or explicitly using <constant>SODIUM_CRYPTO_PWHASH_ALG_ARGON2ID13</constant>, representing the Argon2id algorithm version 1.3.
     </simpara>
    </listitem>
   </varlistentry>
  </variablelist>
 </refsect1>

 <refsect1 role="returnvalues">
  &reftitle.returnvalues;
  <simpara>
   Returns the derived key. The return value is a binary string of the hash, not an ASCII-encoded representation, and does not contain additional information about the parameters used to create the hash, so you will need to keep that information if you are ever going to verify the password in future. Use <function>sodium_crypto_pwhash_str</function> to avoid needing to do all that.
  </simpara>
 </refsect1>
 <refsect1 role="examples">
  &reftitle.examples;
  <example>
   <title><function>sodium_crypto_pwhash</function> example</title>
   <programlisting role="php">
<![CDATA[
<?php
//Need to keep the salt if we're ever going to be able to check this password
$salt = random_bytes(SODIUM_CRYPTO_PWHASH_SALTBYTES);
//Using bin2hex to keep output readable
echo bin2hex(
    sodium_crypto_pwhash(
        16, // == 128 bits
        'password',
        $salt,
        SODIUM_CRYPTO_PWHASH_OPSLIMIT_INTERACTIVE,
        SODIUM_CRYPTO_PWHASH_MEMLIMIT_INTERACTIVE,
        SODIUM_CRYPTO_PWHASH_ALG_ARGON2ID13
    )
);
?>]]>
   </programlisting>
   &example.outputs.similar;
   <screen>
<![CDATA[
a18f346ba57992eb7e4ae6abf3fd30ee
]]>
   </screen>
  </example>
 </refsect1>

</refentry>

<refentry xmlns="http://docbook.org/ns/docbook" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink" xml:id="function.sodium-crypto-scalarmult">
 <refnamediv>
  <refname>sodium_crypto_scalarmult</refname>
  <refpurpose>Compute a shared secret given a user's secret key and another user's public key</refpurpose>
 </refnamediv>

 <refsect1 role="description">
  &reftitle.description;
  <methodsynopsis>
   <type>string</type><methodname>sodium_crypto_scalarmult</methodname>
   <methodparam><type>string</type><parameter>n</parameter></methodparam>
   <methodparam><type>string</type><parameter>p</parameter></methodparam>
  </methodsynopsis>
  <simpara>
   Elliptic Curve Diffie-Hellman. Calculates scalar n times point p, on an elliptic curve.
  </simpara>

 </refsect1>

 <refsect1 role="parameters">
  &reftitle.parameters;
  <variablelist>
   <varlistentry>
    <term><parameter>n</parameter></term>
    <listitem>
     <simpara>
      scalar, which is typically a secret key
     </simpara>
    </listitem>
   </varlistentry>
   <varlistentry>
    <term><parameter>p</parameter></term>
    <listitem>
     <simpara>
      point (x-coordinate), which is typically a public key
     </simpara>
    </listitem>
   </varlistentry>
  </variablelist>
 </refsect1>

 <refsect1 role="returnvalues">
  &reftitle.returnvalues;
  <simpara>
   A 32-byte random string.
  </simpara>
 </refsect1>

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8"?>
<!-- $Revision$ -->
<refentry xmlns="http://docbook.org/ns/docbook" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink" xml:id="function.sodium-crypto-secretbox-keygen">
 <refnamediv>
  <refname>sodium_crypto_secretbox_keygen</refname>
  <refpurpose>Generate random key for sodium_crypto_secretbox</refpurpose>
 </refnamediv>

 <refsect1 role="description">
  &reftitle.description;
  <methodsynopsis>
   <type>string</type><methodname>sodium_crypto_secretbox_keygen</methodname>
   <void/>
  </methodsynopsis>
  <simpara>
   Generate a key for use with <function>sodium_crypto_secretbox</function> and <function>sodium_crypto_secretbox_open</function>.
  </simpara>
 </refsect1>

 <refsect1 role="parameters">
  &reftitle.parameters;
  &no.function.parameters;
 </refsect1>

 <refsect1 role="returnvalues">
  &reftitle.returnvalues;
  <simpara>
   Returns the generated string of cryptographically secure random bytes.
  </simpara>
 </refsect1>

 <refsect1 role="examples">
  &reftitle.examples;
  <para>
   <example>
    <title><function>sodium_crypto_secretbox_keygen</function> example</title>
    <programlisting role="php">
<![CDATA[
<?php
$key = sodium_crypto_secretbox_keygen();
var_dump( sodium_bin2hex( $key ) );
?>
]]>
    </programlisting>
    &example.outputs.similar;
    <screen>
<![CDATA[
string(64) "88bd1dc51ec81984f3ddc5a8f59a3d95b647e2da3e879f1b9ceb0abd89e7286c"
]]>
    </screen>
   </example>

   <example>
    <title>
     Comparing <function>sodium_crypto_secretbox_keygen</function>
     with <function>random_bytes</function>
    </title>
    <programlisting role="php">
<![CDATA[
<?php
$key = sodium_crypto_secretbox_keygen();
$bytes = random_bytes( SODIUM_CRYPTO_SECRETBOX_KEYBYTES );
var_dump( mb_strlen( $key, '8bit' ) === mb_strlen( $bytes, '8bit' ) );
?>
]]>
    </programlisting>
    &example.outputs;
    <screen>
<![CDATA[
bool(true)
]]>
    </screen>
   </example>
  </para>
 </refsect1>

 <refsect1 role="seealso">
  &reftitle.seealso;
  <simplelist>
   <member><function>sodium_bin2hex</function></member>
   <member><function>random_bytes</function></member>
  </simplelist>
 </refsect1>

</refentry>

---

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8"?>
<!-- $Revision$ -->
<refentry xmlns="http://docbook.org/ns/docbook" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink" xml:id="function.sodium-crypto-secretbox-open">
 <refnamediv>
  <refname>sodium_crypto_secretbox_open</refname>
  <refpurpose>Authenticated shared-key decryption</refpurpose>
 </refnamediv>

 <refsect1 role="description">
  &reftitle.description;
  <methodsynopsis>
   <type class="union"><type>string</type><type>false</type></type><methodname>sodium_crypto_secretbox_open</methodname>
   <methodparam><type>string</type><parameter>ciphertext</parameter></methodparam>
   <methodparam><type>string</type><parameter>nonce</parameter></methodparam>
   <methodparam><modifier role="attribute">#[\SensitiveParameter]</modifier><type>string</type><parameter>key</parameter></methodparam>
  </methodsynopsis>
  <simpara>
   Decrypt an encrypted message with a symmetric (shared) key.
  </simpara>

 </refsect1>

 <refsect1 role="parameters">
  &reftitle.parameters;
  <variablelist>
   <varlistentry>
    <term><parameter>ciphertext</parameter></term>
    <listitem>
     <simpara>
      Must be in the format provided by <function>sodium_crypto_secretbox</function>
      (ciphertext and tag, concatenated).
     </simpara>
    </listitem>
   </varlistentry>
   <varlistentry>
    <term><parameter>nonce</parameter></term>
    <listitem>
     <simpara>
      A number that must be only used once, per message. 24 bytes long.
      This is a large enough bound to generate randomly (i.e. <function>random_bytes</function>).
     </simpara>
    </listitem>
   </varlistentry>
   <varlistentry>
    <term><parameter>key</parameter></term>
    <listitem>
     <simpara>
      Encryption key (256-bit).
     </simpara>
    </listitem>
   </varlistentry>
  </variablelist>
 </refsect1>

 <refsect1 role="returnvalues">
  &reftitle.returnvalues;
  <simpara>
   The decrypted string on success&return.falseforfailure;.
  </simpara>
 </refsect1>

 <refsect1 role="errors">
  &reftitle.errors;
  <itemizedlist>
   <listitem>
    <simpara>
     If <parameter>nonce</parameter> has a length of bytes different than
     <link linkend="constant.sodium-crypto-secretbox-noncebytes"><constant>SODIUM_CRYPTO_SECRETBOX_NONCEBYTES</constant></link>
     (24 bytes), a <classname>SodiumException</classname> will be thrown.
    </simpara>
   </listitem>
   <listitem>
    <simpara>
     If <parameter>key</parameter> has a length of bytes different than
     <link linkend="constant.sodium-crypto-secretbox-keybytes"><constant>SODIUM_CRYPTO_SECRETBOX_KEYBYTES</constant></link>
     (32 bytes), a <classname>SodiumException</classname> will be thrown.
    </simpara>
   </listitem>
  </itemizedlist>
 </refsect1>

 <refsect1 role="examples">
  &reftitle.examples;
  <example>
   <title><function>sodium_crypto_secretbox_open</function> example</title>
   <programlisting role="php">
<![CDATA[
<?php
// The $key must be kept confidential
$key = random_bytes(SODIUM_CRYPTO_SECRETBOX_KEYBYTES);
// Do not reuse $nonce with the same key
$nonce = random_bytes(SODIUM_CRYPTO_SECRETBOX_NONCEBYTES);
$ciphertext = sodium_crypto_secretbox('message to be encrypted', $nonce, $key);

// The same nonce and key are required to decrypt the $ciphertext
$plaintext = sodium_crypto_secretbox_open($ciphertext, $nonce, $key);
if ($plaintext !== false) {
    echo $plaintext . PHP_EOL;
}
?>
]]>
   </programlisting>
   &example.outputs;
   <screen>
<![CDATA[
message to be encrypted
]]>
   </screen>
  </example>
 </refsect1>

 </refsect1>

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8"?>
<!-- $Revision$ -->
<refentry xmlns="http://docbook.org/ns/docbook" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink" xml:id="function.sodium-crypto-secretbox">
 <refnamediv>
  <refname>sodium_crypto_secretbox</refname>
  <refpurpose>Authenticated shared-key encryption</refpurpose>
 </refnamediv>

 <refsect1 role="description">
  &reftitle.description;
  <methodsynopsis>
   <type>string</type><methodname>sodium_crypto_secretbox</methodname>
   <methodparam><modifier role="attribute">#[\SensitiveParameter]</modifier><type>string</type><parameter>message</parameter></methodparam>
   <methodparam><type>string</type><parameter>nonce</parameter></methodparam>
   <methodparam><modifier role="attribute">#[\SensitiveParameter]</modifier><type>string</type><parameter>key</parameter></methodparam>
  </methodsynopsis>
  <simpara>
   Encrypt a message with a symmetric (shared) key.
  </simpara>

 </refsect1>

 <refsect1 role="parameters">
  &reftitle.parameters;
  <variablelist>
   <varlistentry>
    <term><parameter>message</parameter></term>
    <listitem>
     <simpara>
      The plaintext message to encrypt.
     </simpara>
    </listitem>
   </varlistentry>
   <varlistentry>
    <term><parameter>nonce</parameter></term>
    <listitem>
     <simpara>
      A number that must be only used once, per message. 24 bytes long.
      This is a large enough bound to generate randomly (i.e. <function>random_bytes</function>).
     </simpara>
    </listitem>
   </varlistentry>
   <varlistentry>
    <term><parameter>key</parameter></term>
    <listitem>
     <simpara>
      Encryption key (256-bit).
     </simpara>
    </listitem>
   </varlistentry>
  </variablelist>
 </refsect1>

 <refsect1 role="returnvalues">
  &reftitle.returnvalues;
  <simpara>
   Returns the encrypted string.
  </simpara>
 </refsect1>

 <refsect1 role="errors">
  &reftitle.errors;
  <itemizedlist>
   <listitem>
    <simpara>
     If <parameter>nonce</parameter> has a length of bytes different than
     <link linkend="constant.sodium-crypto-secretbox-noncebytes"><constant>SODIUM_CRYPTO_SECRETBOX_NONCEBYTES</constant></link>
     (24 bytes), a <classname>SodiumException</classname> will be thrown.
    </simpara>
   </listitem>
   <listitem>
    <simpara>
     If <parameter>key</parameter> has a length of bytes different than
     <link linkend="constant.sodium-crypto-secretbox-keybytes"><constant>SODIUM_CRYPTO_SECRETBOX_KEYBYTES</constant></link>
     (32 bytes), a <classname>SodiumException</classname> will be thrown.
    </simpara>
   </listitem>
   <listitem>
    <simpara>
     Throws a <classname>SodiumException</classname> on failure.
    </simpara>
   </listitem>
  </itemizedlist>
 </refsect1>

 <refsect1 role="examples">
  &reftitle.examples;
  <example>
   <title><function>sodium_crypto_secretbox</function> example</title>
   <programlisting role="php">
<![CDATA[
<?php
// The $key must be kept confidential
$key = sodium_crypto_secretbox_keygen();
// Do not reuse $nonce with the same key
$nonce = random_bytes(SODIUM_CRYPTO_SECRETBOX_NONCEBYTES);
$plaintext = "message to be encrypted";
$ciphertext = sodium_crypto_secretbox($plaintext, $nonce, $key);

var_dump(bin2hex($ciphertext));
// The same nonce and key are required to decrypt the $ciphertext
var_dump(sodium_crypto_secretbox_open($ciphertext, $nonce, $key));
?>
]]>
   </programlisting>
   &example.outputs.similar;
   <screen>
<![CDATA[
string(78) "3a1fa3e9f7b72ef8be51d40abf8e296c6899c185d07b18b4c93e7f26aa776d24c50852cd6b1076"
string(23) "message to be encrypted"
]]>
   </screen>
  </example>
 </refsect1>

 <refsect1 role="seealso">
  &reftitle.seealso;
  <simplelist>
   <member><function>sodium_crypto_secretbox_open</function></member>
   <member><function>sodium_crypto_secretbox_keygen</function></member>
   <member><function>random_bytes</function></member>
  </simplelist>
 </refsect1>

</refentry>

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8"?>
<!-- $Revision$ -->
<refentry xmlns="http://docbook.org/ns/docbook" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink" xml:id="function.sodium-crypto-secretstream-xchacha20poly1305-init-pull">
 <refnamediv>
  <refname>sodium_crypto_secretstream_xchacha20poly1305_init_pull</refname>
  <refpurpose>Initialize a secretstream context for decryption</refpurpose>
 </refnamediv>

 <refsect1 role="description">
  &reftitle.description;
  <methodsynopsis>
   <type>string</type><methodname>sodium_crypto_secretstream_xchacha20poly1305_init_pull</methodname>
   <methodparam><type>string</type><parameter>header</parameter></methodparam>
   <methodparam><modifier role="attribute">#[\SensitiveParameter]</modifier><type>string</type><parameter>key</parameter></methodparam>
  </methodsynopsis>
  <simpara>
   Initialize a secretstream context for decryption.
  </simpara>

 </refsect1>

 <refsect1 role="parameters">
  &reftitle.parameters;
  <variablelist>
   <varlistentry>
    <term><parameter>header</parameter></term>
    <listitem>
     <simpara>
      The header of the secretstream. This should be one of the values produced by
      <function>sodium_crypto_secretstream_xchacha20poly1305_init_push</function>.
     </simpara>
    </listitem>
   </varlistentry>
   <varlistentry>
    <term><parameter>key</parameter></term>
    <listitem>
     <simpara>
      Encryption key (256-bit).
     </simpara>
    </listitem>
   </varlistentry>
  </variablelist>
 </refsect1>

 <refsect1 role="returnvalues">
  &reftitle.returnvalues;
  <simpara>
   Secretstream state.
  </simpara>
 </refsect1>

 <refsect1 role="examples"><!-- {{{ -->
  &reftitle.examples;
  <example xml:id="sodium-crypto-secretstream-xchacha20poly1305-init-pull.example.basic"><!-- {{{ -->
   <title><function>sodium_crypto_secretstream_xchacha20poly1305_init_pull</function> example</title>
   <programlisting role="php">
<![CDATA[
<?php
function decrypt_file(string $inputFilePath, string $outputFilePath, string $key): void
{
    $inputFile = fopen($inputFilePath, 'rb');
    $outputFile = fopen($outputFilePath, 'wb');
    $header = fread($inputFile, 24);

    $state = sodium_crypto_secretstream_xchacha20poly1305_init_pull($header, $key);
    $inputFileSize = fstat($inputFile)['size'];

    // Decrypt the file and write its contents to the output file:
    for ($i = 24; $i < $inputFileSize; $i += 8192) {
        $ctxt_chunk = fread($inputFile, 8192);

        // We're not using $tag, but in real protocols you can use this on encrypt to e.g.
        // trigger a re-key or indicate the end of file. Then, on decrypt, you can assert
        // this behavior.
        [$ptxt_chunk, $tag] = sodium_crypto_secretstream_xchacha20poly1305_pull($state, $ctxt_chunk);
        fwrite($outputFile, $ptxt_chunk);
    }

    sodium_memzero($state);
    fclose($inputFile);
    fclose($outputFile);
}

// sodium_crypto_secretstream_xchacha20poly1305_keygen()
$key = sodium_base642bin('MS0lzb7HC+thY6jY01pkTE/cwsQxnRq0/2L1eL4Hxn8=', SODIUM_BASE64_VARIANT_ORIGINAL);

$example = sodium_hex2bin('971e33b255f0990ef3931caf761c59136efa77b434832f28ec719e3ff73f5aec38b3bba1574ab5b70a8844d8da36a668e802cfea2c');
file_put_contents('hello.enc', $example);
decrypt_file('hello.enc', 'hello.txt.decrypted', $key);
var_dump(file_get_contents('hello.txt.decrypted'));
?>
]]>
   </programlisting>
   &example.outputs.similar;
   <screen>
<![CDATA[
string(12) "Hello world!"
]]>
   </screen>
  </example><!-- }}} -->
 </refsect1><!-- }}} -->
</refentry>

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8"?>
<!-- $Revision$ -->
<refentry xmlns="http://docbook.org/ns/docbook" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink" xml:id="function.sodium-crypto-secretstream-xchacha20poly1305-init-push">
 <refnamediv>
  <refname>sodium_crypto_secretstream_xchacha20poly1305_init_push</refname>
  <refpurpose>Initialize a secretstream context for encryption</refpurpose>
 </refnamediv>

 <refsect1 role="description">
  &reftitle.description;
  <methodsynopsis>
   <type>array</type><methodname>sodium_crypto_secretstream_xchacha20poly1305_init_push</methodname>
   <methodparam><modifier role="attribute">#[\SensitiveParameter]</modifier><type>string</type><parameter>key</parameter></methodparam>
  </methodsynopsis>
  <simpara>
   Initialize a secretstream context for encryption.
  </simpara>

 </refsect1>

 <refsect1 role="parameters">
  &reftitle.parameters;
  <variablelist>
   <varlistentry>
    <term><parameter>key</parameter></term>
    <listitem>
     <simpara>
      Cryptography key. See <function>sodium_crypto_secretstream_xchacha20poly1305_keygen</function>.
     </simpara>
    </listitem>
   </varlistentry>
  </variablelist>
 </refsect1>

 <refsect1 role="returnvalues">
  &reftitle.returnvalues;
  <simpara>
   An array with two string values:
  </simpara>
  <simplelist>
   <member>The secretstream state, needed for further pushes</member>
   <member>The secretstream header, which needs to be provided to the recipient so they can pull data</member>
  </simplelist>
 </refsect1>

 <refsect1 role="examples"><!-- {{{ -->
  &reftitle.examples;
  <example xml:id="sodium-crypto-secretstream-xchacha20poly1305-init-push.example.basic"><!-- {{{ -->
   <title><function>sodium_crypto_secretstream_xchacha20poly1305_init_push</function> example</title>
   <programlisting role="php">
<![CDATA[
<?php
function encrypt_file(string $inputFilePath, string $outputFilePath, string $key): void
{
    [$state, $header] = sodium_crypto_secretstream_xchacha20poly1305_init_push($key);

    $inputFile = fopen($inputFilePath, 'rb');
    $outputFile = fopen($outputFilePath, 'wb');
    // Write the header:
    fwrite($outputFile, $header);
    $inputFileSize = fstat($inputFile)['size'];

    // Encrypt the file and write its contents to the output file:
    for ($i = 0; $i < $inputFileSize; $i += 8175) {
        $ptxt_chunk = fread($inputFile, 8175);
        $ctxt_chunk = sodium_crypto_secretstream_xchacha20poly1305_push($state, $ptxt_chunk);
        fwrite($outputFile, $ctxt_chunk);
    }

    sodium_memzero($state);
    fclose($inputFile);
    fclose($outputFile);
}

// sodium_crypto_secretstream_xchacha20poly1305_keygen()
$key = sodium_base642bin('MS0lzb7HC+thY6jY01pkTE/cwsQxnRq0/2L1eL4Hxn8=', SODIUM_BASE64_VARIANT_ORIGINAL);

file_put_contents('hello.txt', 'Hello world!');
encrypt_file('hello.txt', 'hello.txt.encrypted', $key);
var_dump(sodium_bin2hex(file_get_contents('hello.txt.encrypted')));
?>
]]>
   </programlisting>

]]>
   </screen>

 </refsect1><!-- }}} -->

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8"?>
<!-- $Revision$ -->
<refentry xmlns="http://docbook.org/ns/docbook" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink" xml:id="function.sodium-crypto-secretstream-xchacha20poly1305-pull">
 <refnamediv>
  <refname>sodium_crypto_secretstream_xchacha20poly1305_pull</refname>
  <refpurpose>Decrypt a chunk of data from an encrypted stream</refpurpose>
 </refnamediv>

 <refsect1 role="description">
  &reftitle.description;
  <methodsynopsis>
   <type class="union"><type>array</type><type>false</type></type><methodname>sodium_crypto_secretstream_xchacha20poly1305_pull</methodname>
   <methodparam><type>string</type><parameter role="reference">state</parameter></methodparam>
   <methodparam><type>string</type><parameter>ciphertext</parameter></methodparam>
   <methodparam choice="opt"><type>string</type><parameter>additional_data</parameter><initializer>""</initializer></methodparam>
  </methodsynopsis>
  <simpara>
   Decrypt a chunk of data from an encrypted stream.
  </simpara>

 </refsect1>

 <refsect1 role="parameters">
  &reftitle.parameters;
  <variablelist>
   <varlistentry>
    <term><parameter>state</parameter></term>
    <listitem>
     <simpara>
      See <function>sodium_crypto_secretstream_xchacha20poly1305_init_pull</function>
      and <function>sodium_crypto_secretstream_xchacha20poly1305_init_push</function>
     </simpara>
    </listitem>
   </varlistentry>
   <varlistentry>
    <term><parameter>ciphertext</parameter></term>
    <listitem>
     <simpara>
      The ciphertext chunk to decrypt.
     </simpara>
    </listitem>
   </varlistentry>
   <varlistentry>
    <term><parameter>additional_data</parameter></term>
    <listitem>
     <simpara>
      Optional additional data to include in the authentication tag.
     </simpara>
    </listitem>
   </varlistentry>
  </variablelist>
 </refsect1>

 <refsect1 role="returnvalues">
  &reftitle.returnvalues;
  <para>
   An array with two values:
   <itemizedlist>
    <listitem>
     <simpara>
      <type>string</type>; The decrypted chunk
     </simpara>
    </listitem>
    <listitem>
     <para>
      <type>int</type>; An optional tag (if provided during push). Possible values:
      <simplelist>
       <member>
        <constant>SODIUM_CRYPTO_SECRETSTREAM_XCHACHA20POLY1305_TAG_MESSAGE</constant>:
        the most common tag, that doesn't add any information about the nature of the message.
       </member>
       <member>
        <constant>SODIUM_CRYPTO_SECRETSTREAM_XCHACHA20POLY1305_TAG_FINAL</constant>:
        indicates that the message marks the end of the stream, and erases the secret key used to encrypt the previous sequence.
       </member>
       <member>
        <constant>SODIUM_CRYPTO_SECRETSTREAM_XCHACHA20POLY1305_TAG_PUSH</constant>:
        indicates that the message marks the end of a set of messages, but not the end of the stream.
        For example, a huge JSON string sent as multiple chunks can use this tag to indicate to the application that the
        string is complete and that it can be decoded. But the stream itself is not closed, and more data may follow.
       </member>
       <member>
        <constant>SODIUM_CRYPTO_SECRETSTREAM_XCHACHA20POLY1305_TAG_REKEY</constant>:
        "forget" the key used to encrypt this message and the previous ones, and derive a new secret key.
       </member>
      </simplelist>
     </para>
    </listitem>
   </itemizedlist>
  </para>
 </refsect1>

</refentry>

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8"?>
<!-- $Revision$ -->
<refentry xmlns="http://docbook.org/ns/docbook" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink" xml:id="function.sodium-crypto-secretstream-xchacha20poly1305-push">
 <refnamediv>
  <refname>sodium_crypto_secretstream_xchacha20poly1305_push</refname>
  <refpurpose>Encrypt a chunk of data so that it can safely be decrypted in a streaming API</refpurpose>
 </refnamediv>

 <refsect1 role="description">
  &reftitle.description;
  <methodsynopsis>
   <type>string</type><methodname>sodium_crypto_secretstream_xchacha20poly1305_push</methodname>
   <methodparam><type>string</type><parameter role="reference">state</parameter></methodparam>
   <methodparam><modifier role="attribute">#[\SensitiveParameter]</modifier><type>string</type><parameter>message</parameter></methodparam>
   <methodparam choice="opt"><type>string</type><parameter>additional_data</parameter><initializer>""</initializer></methodparam>
   <methodparam choice="opt"><type>int</type><parameter>tag</parameter><initializer><constant>SODIUM_CRYPTO_SECRETSTREAM_XCHACHA20POLY1305_TAG_MESSAGE</constant></initializer></methodparam>
  </methodsynopsis>
  <simpara>
   Encrypt a chunk of data so that it can safely be decrypted in a streaming API.
  </simpara>

 </refsect1>

 <refsect1 role="parameters">
  &reftitle.parameters;
  <variablelist>
   <varlistentry>
    <term><parameter>state</parameter></term>
    <listitem>
     <simpara>
      See <function>sodium_crypto_secretstream_xchacha20poly1305_init_pull</function>
      and <function>sodium_crypto_secretstream_xchacha20poly1305_init_push</function>
     </simpara>
    </listitem>
   </varlistentry>
   <varlistentry>
    <term><parameter>message</parameter></term>
    <listitem>
     <simpara>

     </simpara>
    </listitem>
   </varlistentry>
   <varlistentry>
    <term><parameter>additional_data</parameter></term>
    <listitem>
     <simpara>

     </simpara>
    </listitem>
   </varlistentry>
   <varlistentry>
    <term><parameter>tag</parameter></term>
    <listitem>
     <simpara>
      Optional. Can be used to assert decryption behavior
      (i.e. re-keying or indicating the final chunk in a stream).
     </simpara>
     <simplelist>
      <member>
       <constant>SODIUM_CRYPTO_SECRETSTREAM_XCHACHA20POLY1305_TAG_MESSAGE</constant>:
       the most common tag, that doesn't add any information about the nature of the message.
      </member>
      <member>
       <constant>SODIUM_CRYPTO_SECRETSTREAM_XCHACHA20POLY1305_TAG_FINAL</constant>:
       indicates that the message marks the end of the stream, and erases the secret key used to encrypt the previous sequence.
      </member>
      <member>
       <constant>SODIUM_CRYPTO_SECRETSTREAM_XCHACHA20POLY1305_TAG_PUSH</constant>:
       indicates that the message marks the end of a set of messages, but not the end of the stream.
       For example, a huge JSON string sent as multiple chunks can use this tag to indicate to the application that the
       string is complete and that it can be decoded. But the stream itself is not closed, and more data may follow.
      </member>
      <member>
       <constant>SODIUM_CRYPTO_SECRETSTREAM_XCHACHA20POLY1305_TAG_REKEY</constant>:
       "forget" the key used to encrypt this message and the previous ones, and derive a new secret key.
      </member>
     </simplelist>
    </listitem>
   </varlistentry>
  </variablelist>
 </refsect1>

 <refsect1 role="returnvalues">
  &reftitle.returnvalues;
  <simpara>
   Returns the encrypted ciphertext.
  </simpara>
 </refsect1>


</refentry>

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8"?>
<!-- $Revision$ -->
<refentry xmlns="http://docbook.org/ns/docbook" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink" xml:id="function.sodium-crypto-shorthash">
 <refnamediv>
  <refname>sodium_crypto_shorthash</refname>
  <refpurpose>Compute a short hash of a message and key</refpurpose>
 </refnamediv>

 <refsect1 role="description">
  &reftitle.description;
  <methodsynopsis>
   <type>string</type><methodname>sodium_crypto_shorthash</methodname>
   <methodparam><type>string</type><parameter>message</parameter></methodparam>
   <methodparam><modifier role="attribute">#[\SensitiveParameter]</modifier><type>string</type><parameter>key</parameter></methodparam>
  </methodsynopsis>
  <simpara>
   <function>sodium_crypto_shorthash</function> wraps a hash function called
   SipHash-2-4, which is ideal for implementing hash tables that are not susceptible
   to hash collision denial of service attacks (Hash-DoS).
  </simpara>
  <simpara>
   SipHash-2-4 isn't a general purpose cryptographic hash function.
  </simpara>

 </refsect1>

 <refsect1 role="parameters">
  &reftitle.parameters;
  <variablelist>
   <varlistentry>
    <term><parameter>message</parameter></term>
    <listitem>
     <simpara>
      The message to hash.
     </simpara>
    </listitem>
   </varlistentry>
   <varlistentry>
    <term><parameter>key</parameter></term>
    <listitem>
     <simpara>
      The hash key.
     </simpara>
    </listitem>
   </varlistentry>
  </variablelist>
 </refsect1>

 <refsect1 role="returnvalues">
  &reftitle.returnvalues;
  <simpara>

  </simpara>
 </refsect1>


</refentry>

<refentry xmlns="http://docbook.org/ns/docbook" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink" xml:id="function.sodium-crypto-sign-open">
 <refnamediv>
  <refname>sodium_crypto_sign_open</refname>
  <refpurpose>Check that the signed message has a valid signature</refpurpose>
 </refnamediv>

 <refsect1 role="description">
  &reftitle.description;
  <methodsynopsis>
   <type class="union"><type>string</type><type>false</type></type><methodname>sodium_crypto_sign_open</methodname>
   <methodparam><type>string</type><parameter>signed_message</parameter></methodparam>
   <methodparam><type>string</type><parameter>public_key</parameter></methodparam>
  </methodsynopsis>
  <simpara>
   Verify the signature attached to a message and return the message
  </simpara>

 </refsect1>

 <refsect1 role="parameters">
  &reftitle.parameters;
  <variablelist>
   <varlistentry>

     <simpara>
      A message signed with <function>sodium_crypto_sign</function>
     </simpara>
    </listitem>
   </varlistentry>
   <varlistentry>
    <term><parameter>public_key</parameter></term>
    <listitem>
     <simpara>

    </listitem>
   </varlistentry>
  </variablelist>
 </refsect1>

  </simpara>

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8"?>
<!-- $Revision$ -->
<refentry xmlns="http://docbook.org/ns/docbook" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink" xml:id="function.sodium-crypto-sign-seed-keypair">
 <refnamediv>
  <refname>sodium_crypto_sign_seed_keypair</refname>
  <refpurpose>Deterministically derive the key pair from a single key</refpurpose>
 </refnamediv>

 <refsect1 role="description">
  &reftitle.description;
  <methodsynopsis>
   <type>string</type><methodname>sodium_crypto_sign_seed_keypair</methodname>
   <methodparam><modifier role="attribute">#[\SensitiveParameter]</modifier><type>string</type><parameter>seed</parameter></methodparam>
  </methodsynopsis>
  <simpara>
   Clamps the seed to form a secret key, derives the public key, and returns the two as a keypair.
  </simpara>
  <simpara>
   The <literal>*_seed_keypair</literal> functions are ideal for generating a keypair from a
   password and salt. Use the result as a <parameter>seed</parameter> to generate the desired keys.
  </simpara>

 </refsect1>

 <refsect1 role="parameters">
  &reftitle.parameters;
  <variablelist>
   <varlistentry>
    <term><parameter>seed</parameter></term>
    <listitem>
     <simpara>
      Some cryptographic input. Must be 32 bytes.
     </simpara>
    </listitem>
   </varlistentry>
  </variablelist>
 </refsect1>

 <refsect1 role="returnvalues">
  &reftitle.returnvalues;
  <simpara>
   Keypair (secret key and public key)
  </simpara>
 </refsect1>


</refentry>

<!-- $Revision$ -->
<refentry xmlns="http://docbook.org/ns/docbook" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink" xml:id="function.sodium-crypto-sign">
 <refnamediv>
  <refname>sodium_crypto_sign</refname>
  <refpurpose>Sign a message</refpurpose>
 </refnamediv>

 <refsect1 role="description">
  &reftitle.description;
  <methodsynopsis>
   <type>string</type><methodname>sodium_crypto_sign</methodname>
   <methodparam><type>string</type><parameter>message</parameter></methodparam>
   <methodparam><modifier role="attribute">#[\SensitiveParameter]</modifier><type>string</type><parameter>secret_key</parameter></methodparam>
  </methodsynopsis>
  <simpara>
   Sign a message with a secret key, that can be verified by the corresponding public key.
   This function attaches the signature to the message. See <function>sodium_crypto_sign_detached</function>
   for detached signatures.
  </simpara>

 </refsect1>

 <refsect1 role="parameters">
  &reftitle.parameters;
  <variablelist>
   <varlistentry>
    <term><parameter>message</parameter></term>
    <listitem>
     <simpara>
      Message to sign.
     </simpara>
    </listitem>
   </varlistentry>
   <varlistentry>
    <term><parameter>secret_key</parameter></term>
    <listitem>
     <simpara>
      Secret key. See <function>sodium_crypto_sign_secretkey</function>
     </simpara>
    </listitem>
   </varlistentry>
  </variablelist>
 </refsect1>

 <refsect1 role="returnvalues">
  &reftitle.returnvalues;
  <simpara>
   Signed message (not encrypted).
  </simpara>
 </refsect1>


</refentry>

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8"?>
<refentry xmlns="http://docbook.org/ns/docbook" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink" xml:id="function.sodium-crypto-stream-xchacha20-xor-ic">
 <refnamediv>
  <refname>sodium_crypto_stream_xchacha20_xor_ic</refname>
  <refpurpose>Encrypts a message using a nonce and a secret key (no authentication)</refpurpose>
 </refnamediv>

 <refsect1 role="description">
  &reftitle.description;
  <methodsynopsis>
   <type>string</type><methodname>sodium_crypto_stream_xchacha20_xor_ic</methodname>
   <methodparam><modifier role="attribute">#[\SensitiveParameter]</modifier><type>string</type><parameter>message</parameter></methodparam>
   <methodparam><type>string</type><parameter>nonce</parameter></methodparam>
   <methodparam><type>int</type><parameter>counter</parameter></methodparam>
   <methodparam><modifier role="attribute">#[\SensitiveParameter]</modifier><type>string</type><parameter>key</parameter></methodparam>
  </methodsynopsis>
  <simpara>
   The function is similar to <function>sodium_crypto_stream_xchacha20_xor</function>
   but adds the ability to set the initial value of the block counter to a non-zero value.
   This permits direct access to any block without having to compute the previous ones.
  </simpara>

  <caution>
   <simpara>
    This encryption is unauthenticated, and does not prevent chosen-ciphertext attacks.
    Make sure to combine the ciphertext with a Message Authentication Code,
    for example with <function>sodium_crypto_aead_xchacha20poly1305_ietf_encrypt</function> function,
    or <function>sodium_crypto_auth</function>.
   </simpara>
  </caution>
 </refsect1>

 <refsect1 role="parameters">
  &reftitle.parameters;
  <variablelist>
   <varlistentry>
    <term><parameter>message</parameter></term>
    <listitem>
     <simpara>
      The message to encrypt.
     </simpara>
    </listitem>
   </varlistentry>
   <varlistentry>
    <term><parameter>nonce</parameter></term>
    <listitem>
     <simpara>
      24-byte nonce.
     </simpara>
    </listitem>
   </varlistentry>
   <varlistentry>
    <term><parameter>counter</parameter></term>
    <listitem>
     <simpara>
      The initial value of the block counter.
     </simpara>
    </listitem>
   </varlistentry>
   <varlistentry>
    <term><parameter>key</parameter></term>
    <listitem>
     <simpara>
      Key, possibly generated from <function>sodium_crypto_stream_xchacha20_keygen</function>.
     </simpara>
    </listitem>
   </varlistentry>
  </variablelist>
 </refsect1>

 <refsect1 role="returnvalues">
  &reftitle.returnvalues;
  <simpara>
   Encrypted message.
  </simpara>
 </refsect1>

 <refsect1 role="examples">
  &reftitle.examples;
  <example>
   <title><function>sodium_crypto_stream_xchacha20_xor_ic</function> example</title>
   <programlisting role="php">
<![CDATA[
<?php
$n2 = random_bytes(SODIUM_CRYPTO_STREAM_XCHACHA20_NONCEBYTES);
$left  = str_repeat("\x01", 64);
$right = str_repeat("\xfe", 64);

// All at once:
$stream7_unified = sodium_crypto_stream_xchacha20_xor($left . $right, $n2, $key);

// Piecewise, with initial counter:
$stream7_left  = sodium_crypto_stream_xchacha20_xor_ic($left, $n2, 0, $key);
$stream7_right = sodium_crypto_stream_xchacha20_xor_ic($right, $n2, 1, $key);
$stream7_concat = $stream7_left . $stream7_right;

var_dump(strlen($stream7_concat));
var_dump($stream7_unified === $stream7_concat);
?>
]]>
   </programlisting>
   &example.outputs.similar;
   <screen>
<![CDATA[
int(128)
bool(true)
]]>
   </screen>
  </example>
 </refsect1>

 <refsect1 role="seealso">
  &reftitle.seealso;
  <simplelist>
   <member><function>sodium_crypto_stream_xchacha20_xor</function></member>
  </simplelist>
 </refsect1>

</refentry>

 <refnamediv>

 <refsect1 role="description">
  &reftitle.description;
  <methodsynopsis>
   <type>string</type><methodname>sodium_crypto_stream_xor</methodname>

  <simpara>

  </simpara>

 </refsect1>

 <refsect1 role="parameters">
  &reftitle.parameters;
  <variablelist>
   <varlistentry>
    <term><parameter>message</parameter></term>

    </listitem>
   </varlistentry>
   <varlistentry>
    <term><parameter>nonce</parameter></term>

      This is a large enough bound to generate randomly (i.e. <function>random_bytes</function>).

   Encrypted message.
  </simpara>

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8"?>
<!-- $Revision$ -->
<refentry xmlns="http://docbook.org/ns/docbook" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink" xml:id="function.sodium-crypto-stream">
 <refnamediv>
  <refname>sodium_crypto_stream</refname>
  <refpurpose>Generate a deterministic sequence of bytes from a seed</refpurpose>
 </refnamediv>

 <refsect1 role="description">
  &reftitle.description;
  <methodsynopsis>
   <type>string</type><methodname>sodium_crypto_stream</methodname>
   <methodparam><type>int</type><parameter>length</parameter></methodparam>
   <methodparam><type>string</type><parameter>nonce</parameter></methodparam>
   <methodparam><modifier role="attribute">#[\SensitiveParameter]</modifier><type>string</type><parameter>key</parameter></methodparam>
  </methodsynopsis>
  <simpara>
   Generate a deterministic sequence of bytes from a seed, using the XSalsa20 stream cipher.
  </simpara>

 </refsect1>

 <refsect1 role="parameters">
  &reftitle.parameters;
  <variablelist>
   <varlistentry>
    <term><parameter>length</parameter></term>
    <listitem>
     <simpara>
      The number of bytes to return.
     </simpara>
    </listitem>
   </varlistentry>
   <varlistentry>
    <term><parameter>nonce</parameter></term>
    <listitem>
     <simpara>
      A number that must be only used once, per message. 24 bytes long.
      This is a large enough bound to generate randomly (i.e. <function>random_bytes</function>).
     </simpara>
    </listitem>
   </varlistentry>
   <varlistentry>
    <term><parameter>key</parameter></term>
    <listitem>
     <simpara>
      Encryption key (256-bit).
     </simpara>
    </listitem>
   </varlistentry>
  </variablelist>
 </refsect1>

 <refsect1 role="returnvalues">
  &reftitle.returnvalues;
  <simpara>
   String of pseudorandom bytes.
  </simpara>
 </refsect1>


</refentry>
